title: Free version is severely handicapped
body:
The app sounds like a great idea, but the free version is handicapped, which prevents me from experiencing and evaluating if the app is actually useful. 

You can only “track” 10 things in the free version. Most of us interested in this app, would like to track easily more than 10 things in any given week. 

So if you want to track your whole day/week to evaluate the app, you can’t. Unless you track less than 10 things. Already at my limit, I was like, “Oh, ok…I guess I won’t add exercise, and language studying…I’m at the limit already”, and that’s just a pointless state to have your customer in, when you want them to evaluate your app. 

This defeats the purpose of the app, as I want to track my DAILY ROUTINES, and productivity, as opposed to ‘just a part of my day’. So I’m never able to evaluate using this for a full day/week, as I need to go to my older app, to continue tracking the rest of my day? That’s silly. 

There is a free-trial for 7 days, but you have to agree to getting charged 40 bucks, and you have to proactively cancel it, to avoid getting charged. That’s just a habit trap and they know it. They’re literally all about habits! lol Like cancelling a gym subscription. You remember you have to cancel the fee tomorrow, or you get charged, but you forget, and by the time you remember, you’ve already been charged. I dislike this. I’d wager this method is a significant portion of their in-app-purchases. 

Recommendation for dev: Give us full use of the app for 7 or 8 days (to get a FULL week of use), after which the app becomes unusable (or it goes back to the 10 tracking limit), if they decide not to proceed further. 

Fwiw, I’m going to continue to try and track the 10 things I have access to try it out, but those are my honest opinions, and first impressions. Now while I evaluate your app with the 10 item limit, I have to use my other tracking app which doesn’t limit me. You’re already on my annoyed side.   ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

title: Free Version is Great
body:

The only issues I’ve found are that sometimes when you try to remove a habit from your routine, it won’t go away. It also seems that habits that aren’t set up to remind you every day still show up on the “My Routine” tab every day. For example, I take probiotics twice weekly, on Monday and Thursday, but today (Tuesday) my “Take Probiotics” habit is showing incomplete. 

I’d love to see habit sorting options in the “My Routine” tab as well. For example, if I want to exercise at 5:30am and read at 6:30am and I have reminders set accordingly,  it’d be great to have an options to sort those habits chronologically to have a better road map for my day. If this could also be implemented in a widget, I’d put it on my Lock Screen to help me stay on track seeing as I, like many, pick up my phone quite often throughout the day.

All in all, I love the app and I hope that the developers will continue improving the UI. I’m definitely considering the premium version as it stands. I’d just like to see some minor quality of life improvements first.

title: Good habit tracker, but many advertised features missing.
body:
This is a good habit tracker, for sure. I like the interface, and how easy it is to use, and it also has everything that you need to keep track of your life quickly and easily. 

The problem is that there were a lot of features mentioned in the advertisement that convinced me to sign up for it that either aren’t there, or that are significantly worse than one would expect. 

For example, I was told that there was a leaderboard for keeping track of different habits, and that you could compete against other people around the world.  That feature just doesn’t exist. 

Also, the “leveling” system is very disappointing.  I reached the platinum rank within a number of days, and no matter how far I go without doing any of my daily habits, it just stays there.  There are no consequences for sleeping in and missing out. 

Also, the AI recommended habits don’t do a good job of explaining to you why certain habits are chosen over others, or of how it determines whether or not they’re working for you.  That was another major selling point for me, but another disappointment. 

All in all, I would recommend this to a friend as a habit tracker, but I wouldn’t recommend it as a life changing piece of software.  It may be worth a one time purchase, but definitely not a subscription.

title: First Impressions (good and bad) will update
body:
The video on the website sold me on getting this app. Little simplistic for paying $26 considering there’s many apps similar with its functionality and purpose. All it is really is 5 tabs (habit, routine, track habits, dashboard, courses) that’ll you mainly use

Basically it goes like this, choose a habit and learn about it a little bit. Choose a routine that has a collection of habits. Track your habits and just mark the days of the week your doing them. The dashboard would then give you a nice graph of your chosen habits. Once that quickly ends head over to courses tab to be upsold.

There is upselling in the app. It’s to be expected but paying for additional content doesn’t seem worth it partially due to the “Wake Up Without An Alarm” habit they have as one of its first dozen option. The habits description goes into how it’s beneficial and some statistics on sleep patterns. However, the only advice given word for word says

“The first step to reset your brains wiring and gain an incredible mental edge over everyone else is to let your body tell you when to start the day - not your alarm. What about the people in a career field where the day must start at a certain time? There is a solution - can be additional content”

My issues with this statement is 
1. Do y’all not know the solution in the last sentence or are y’all using these habits to bait people into buying more. It’s smart I guess just questionable 
2. There was a lot of words there that could be summed up easily
3. There was ironically a pop up to set a reminder for the habit that encourages me to not wake up with an alarm

Contrary to the negativity

I will say the app is really nice. Smooth to use pretty in color and design and I can tell their being ambitious with their goals as a company. You can definitely learn something from the descriptions and information about the habits offered. 

I would really encourage this app try and make this app more interactive and essential on a day to day basis. Though I’m not 100% satisfied with the purchase but I will keep it as I’m sure it’ll get better
